turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hi, I'm Maya. Leo's with me, and today's section is called Database foundations and relational thinking.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: From stored files to a well-defined relational model.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: explain what a DBMS does, read relations as structured sets, and protect data with keys and integrity rules.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with introduction to DBMS, Data Models, Design Process and work our way to actions Taken by DBMS to Enforce Referential Integrity.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's start with introduction to DBMS, Data Models, Design Process. What do we need to know?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The relational model represents data as relations: sets of tuples described by attributes and domains. A DBMS defines, validates and retrieves this data while separating applications from low-level file handling.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Relation means a set of tuples described by a fixed set of attributes.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Student(id, name, year) describes a relation; one tuple such as (42, “Mina”, 2) is one student record.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A schema describes attributes and rules; one tuple is a record conforming to that schema.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to the Relational Model Concepts & Terminology. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Choose attributes, domains and keys that make each fact identifiable.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Tuple means one row-shaped record in a relation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A table has one row per student and columns id, name and year. What does one row represent?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: One tuple in the Student relation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A relation is a set of allowed combinations drawn from the attribute domains. If the domains are student IDs and names, their Cartesian product contains every possible ID-and-name pair.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: The relation contains only the pairs that are actually recorded. That's the mathematical reason for the name.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: NULL marks a missing or unknown value, rather than a value such as zero or an empty string. If we don't know a student's phone number, comparing it with another number doesn't establish that they match or differ.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: In SQL, use IS NULL to test for the missing marker.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain the Relational Model Keys Candidate Key, Primary to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A superkey identifies a tuple uniquely. A candidate key is a superkey with no unnecessary attributes; removing any part loses the guarantee.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We choose one candidate key as the primary key. Two students may share a name, so a name alone isn't automatically a key.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: State integrity rules so invalid tuples cannot silently enter the database.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Schema means the named attributes and constraints that define a relation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A table has one row per student and columns id, name and year. What does one row represent? What should the learner check next?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: One tuple in the Student relation. Choose attributes, domains and keys that make each fact identifiable.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: CREATE TABLE defines a structure and its constraints. INSERT adds a row, UPDATE changes existing rows, and DELETE removes them.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Those are different jobs: changing a table's definition isn't the same as changing the facts stored inside it.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We also need to talk about integrity Constraints in Relational Model.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Constraints state which database states are allowed. A primary key prevents duplicate identifiers and missing key values.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A domain rule can reject an impossible age. The database checks these rules when data changes, so correctness doesn't depend only on an application's form validation.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A foreign key links a referencing table to a key in another table, or sometimes the same table. If an enrollment names a student ID, that reference must satisfy the declared foreign-key constraint.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: For a non-NULL reference, the corresponding student key must exist.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: What happens if someone deletes a student who still has enrollment records? The declared foreign-key action decides.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A restriction can reject the deletion; cascading can remove the related enrollments. Setting the reference to NULL is another option only when the column permits NULL.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave database foundations and relational thinking, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya

turns.speaker: leo

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Try explaining actions Taken by DBMS to Enforce Referential Integrity in your own words. If you get stuck, that chapter is a good place to listen again.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I'm Maya, and this is CSQuest Audio. Today, Leo and I are taking on Relational algebra.

turns.text: We'll begin with physical, Logical Data Independence and work our way to writing & Understanding Relational Algebra Queries.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: physical, Logical Data Independence.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Data independence means a schema layer can change while the layer above it keeps the same interface. Physical independence hides storage changes from the conceptual schema; logical independence hides selected conceptual changes from external views.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: External schema means a view of the data designed for a user or application.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Adding an index changes an internal access path while the table definition stays the same: that is a physical change.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Splitting a table while preserving an application view illustrates logical independence.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on relational Algebra - Selection, Projection.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Relational algebra is a procedural language for transforming relations into a result relation. Each operator has a clear input and output, so a query can be built and checked one step at a time.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Selection σ means keep tuples that satisfy a predicate.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A query keeps only rows with year = 2 but retains every column. Which operator performs that filtering?

turns.speaker: maya

turns.speaker: maya

turns.speaker: maya

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Project the requested attributes and verify set semantics.

turns.speaker: leo

turns.speaker: maya

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Division answers an every-item question, such as which students took every required course. An outer join solves a different problem: it keeps unmatched rows from one or both inputs and fills missing values on the other side with NULL.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: These operators shouldn't be substituted for one another.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Start with the output the question asks for, then identify which relations hold those facts. Selection filters tuples; projection chooses attributes.

turns.speaker: leo
